rules_text:
Rules summary A Tactical Dice Game by Günter Cornett for 2 players of 8 years and up (Original Translation: Ben Baldanza) What China Gold is about : Both players are searching for gold, one in the mountains and the other in the rivers. If all the gold of a prospecting area of a mountain or a river is found, the mountain or river player can claim the gold. But note that every prospecting area is at the same moment part of a mountain and part of a river. Thus the players are racing to see who can collect the gold first from each area. The Game Board : 12 mountains, 12 rivers and 61 Prospecting Areas are shown on the game board. The Prospecting Areas are represented both as mountains (brown planes) and as rivers (blue lines). Game Play : On each turn, the sum of the random discs indicates how many Prospecting Area Markers may be turned face up. The Prospecting Area Markers to be turned MUST lie side by side in a straight line, without a gap or previously discovered lumps of gold in between. Instead of turning the thrown number of Prospecting Area Markers face up, the player may hide exactly one nugget again by turning one Prospecting Area Marker face down. When the last marker in one of the player's areas (mountain or river) is turned face up, all of the gold in this area can be claimed. If the last Prospecting Area Marker in one of the opponent's areas is turned face up at the same time, the opponent then claims the gold in this area. Small Disc Reduction : Five not yet turned Prospecting Area Markers in a straight line make two different possibilities to turn four Prospecting Area Markers face up. When there is at most one straight line of five Prospecting Area Markers neighboring in straight line that could be turned face up, the small disc 0/1 is returned to the box. For the remainder of the game, small discs 0/2 and 1/2 will be used so that only numbers from 1 to 4 will be available. Four not yet turned Prospecting Area Markers in a straight line make two different possibilities to turn three Prospecting Area Markers face up. When there is at most one straight line of four Prospecting Area Markers neighboring in straight line that could be turned face up, the small disc 0/2 is replaced with the small disc 0/1 from the box so that only numbers from 1 to 3 will be available. If turning back a Prospecting Area Marker creates a situation with more possibilities to turn free Prospecting Area Markers in straight line face up, the appropriate number of small discs is used. When there is at most one straight line of three Prospecting Area Markers neighboring in straight line that could be turned face up, all small discs are returned to the box. From now on the players may choose between turning a single or two neighbouring Prospecting Area Markers face up. Game End : When all Prospecting Areas are cleared, the player who collected the most gold is the winner !

community_text:
[Rating: 4/10] I was hoping that there would be something more to this game.  Roll the wooden "Dice" and see what can happen.  I felt like I was helping my opponent more than I was helping myself.  I am tempted to play this again as red, as every turn I play for blue it seems I can only help red (please don't ask me for the logic to this, I think I just saw the other connections easier).  I suspect that playing this again would improve its standing in my eyes, though will be highly unlikely that I'll get the chance, or perhaps this is just too abstract for me.

[Rating: 4/10] 2 plays.  Feels like a simplified Samurai, where you never want to take your turn because it always seems to help your opponent.  Not fun.  Weird theme.

[Rating: 4/10] I have played this a handful of times online and am kind of done with it. It's basically an abstract with some dice rolls mixed in which isn’t the best combination. It's a very tactical game and the dice rolls can get frustrating at times. The end is anti climactic, in most cases there are no decisions to be made.

[Rating: 4/10] Chinagold is a traditional abstract boardgame that is heavy in tactics and is all about spotting and seizing the opportunities. In short, players are trying to collect gold by revealing tokens in a network of islands and rivers. The player who reveals the last token on an island or in a river claims them all. There is not much room for strategy. The number of tokens you can reveal on your turn is randomly determined and thus your decisions are limited. Basically players only try to spot opportunities to claim tokens, and if that is not possible they try to deny the opponent from making a claim

[Rating: 4/10] An abstract game of flipping over gold in either the forests or the rivers by using dice to flip a straight line of pieces. Once either a forest area or river segment is filled the player that is playing that terrain collects the gold. Most gold wins. It's very tactical because of the dice to determine how many pieces you can flip each turn and as the board empties the decision space becomes very small. Not my first choice for a game on Yucata but it does play nice and quick.

[Rating: 4/10] Wasn't a big fan of dice deciding how many items you could or had to place.  Often the bigger dice rolls were some of the worst results.

[Rating: 4/10] Found on BGA - Just another abstract game. I can see the appeal, but it really doesn't excite me at all. It is a game I will easily forget about by the end of the year and recap and have to remember what this game even is. If you enjoy 2p abstracts this is one that you should try.

[Rating: 4/10] I'm finding Günter Cornett's designs always have some little twist to them which holds my interest. Here is a fairly straightforward area control game where one player is aiming to control rivers, the other mountains, and these two features overlap one another on the hex board. Dice rolls (three d2!) determine how many points a player may flip in a straight line. When all the points on a feature are flipped, the player playing that feature takes all the uncovered gold.  Rated after one play on Yucata. I'd prefer to play something else but perhaps this would be fun in person.
